svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, "Noto Sans SC", "PingFang SC", "Microsoft YaHei", sans-serif
svg.title: Design trade-offs: decision, reason and cost
svg.desc: A comparison of five key decisions, each listing the decision, the benefit it bought and the cost it charged: Core depends on 5 contracts only, entry classes serve the report page themselves, no shared layer is extracted, stubs are checked by an independent verification loop, and the six new frameworks use explicit injection rather than autoDetect.
svg.text: Design Trade-offs: decision → reason → cost
What each of the five decisions bought, and what it charged
changes to src/Core/ from the 6 new frameworks = 0
Decision · what we chose
Reason · what it bought
Cost · what it charged
Core depends on the 5 contract interfaces only
src/Core/ imports only those 5 interfaces,
and imports no framework class
adding a framework = adding one directory
the 6 new frameworks change 0 lines of src/Core/;
Webman/Laravel behaviour is unaffected too
the same contract implemented 11 times
11 frameworks each write 5 Adapters,
the contract holds but the implementation is rewritten
entry classes serve the report page themselves
the entry class checks the path before start; a report-page hit
returns at once with withBody(Xhprof::index())->send()
removes 3 jobs per framework
no controller to write, no report-page route to register,
no asset route to register
the short-circuit logic repeated 11 times
those 3 are exactly where a wrong guess hides from tests,
repetition buys certainty (the Drupal standard module is the exception)
no shared layer extracted
PSR-7 (Yii3 / Slim) and HttpFoundation
(Symfony / Drupal) have the same shape, yet each is implemented separately
frameworks stay fully isolated
changing one framework's adapter cannot reach another,
so shared-file conflicts stay minimal
about 30 near-duplicate adapters
duplication is on the books, drift is off them —
parity tests turn drift into a red light
stubs checked by an independent verification loop
whoever writes an adapter does not write the stubs it depends on,
stubs, signatures and semantics are checked independently
breaks the circular argument
otherwise the stub faithfully encodes the author's guess about the framework API:
unit tests all green, and on a real machine, Call to undefined method
verification depth is uneven
L2 semantics cover 4.5/6; WordPress cannot be covered,
only source-text checks and a manual smoke test
explicit injection rather than autoDetect
all 6 new frameworks use explicit injection:
Xhprof::bootstrap($req, $res, $cfg, $cache, $log)
kills the branch that can never fire
a mistyped probe class name → the branch never fires;
the Hyperf branch in this repo already took that hit once
entry classes must assemble their own adapters
Core no longer probes; each entry class writes
about 30 lines (including 5 adapter constructions)
